title: Listening to Space: Kuntunse

cues.text: When you imagine listening to space, you might picture the sound of a spacecraft moving past the stars.
But space is mostly a vacuum, so ordinary sound cannot travel through it in the way it travels through air on Earth.
Astronomers can still study the universe using radio waves.
Radio waves are a form of electromagnetic radiation.
Unlike ordinary sound, they can travel through the vacuum of space.
Radio telescopes detect radio signals from objects and processes in the universe.
Scientists then analyse these signals to investigate astronomical sources and learn more about the cosmos.
Sometimes, researchers convert measurements into sound so people can listen to patterns in the data.
The sound is a way of representing the data; it is not necessarily the original sound of the astronomical object.
Ghana has an important connection to radio astronomy through the Ghana Radio Astronomy Observatory at Kuntunse, near Accra.
The facility uses a large radio telescope to support astronomical research and related scientific activities.
By studying radio signals, researchers can investigate parts of the universe that are difficult or impossible to study using visible light alone.
